transcript:
User: Hey! So I'm Sofia — I run a real estate office here in Houston. Your ad was talking about missed calls? That's literally me.
Agent: Hey Sofia—got it, you saw our ad about missed calls. What’s been causing the missed calls for you lately: too many incoming at once, after-hours, or not enough staff?
User: Definitely too many calls at once! Oh, and sometimes after-hours. Just can't keep up with it all!
Agent: Makes sense—when too many calls hit at once and some come in after-hours, those calls that go to voicemail… do they usually leave a message, or do they just call the next agent?
User: Honestly, they rarely leave a message. Most likely they move on to the next agent. It's frustrating!
Agent: Ugh, yeah—that’s frustrating, and it usually means the lead’s basically gone once they move on. Roughly how many calls a week would you say end up going to voicemail or getting missed?
User: I don't really track it, but maybe around 25? Or 30? No, actually, I mean 25.
Agent: Got it—about 25 a week is a lot of chances for leads to slip away. When those calls get missed, are they mostly new buyer/seller inquiries, or existing clients calling in?
User: Mostly new buyer/seller inquiries. It's like I'm losing potential deals every single day!
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—if they’re mostly new buyer/seller inquiries and they’re moving on, that’s real deals walking out the door. When you do miss one of those calls, do you have any way to get them back, or are they usually gone?
User: Gone pretty much. I try calling back, but often they’ve already found someone else. It's a mess!
Agent: Yeah—that’s exactly the problem: once they’ve found someone else, the call-back doesn’t really matter. When you say “it’s a mess,” what’s the biggest thing you want fixed first—capturing those new buyer/seller calls during the day, or covering after-hours?
User: Capturing new buyer/seller calls during the day is priority. That's when I miss the most opportunities!
Agent: Got it—daytime buyer/seller calls are the big one. When multiple calls come in at once, what happens right now—do they all ring one main line, or does it route to a few agents?
User: All ring one main line, and it just becomes chaos. We can't juggle it all efficiently.
Agent: Got it—one main line can turn into chaos fast. When it gets like that, what usually happens to the overflow calls—do they just ring out to voicemail, or does someone try to grab them and put them on hold?
User: Voicemail mostly, but sometimes we scramble to pick up and put them on hold. It's hectic.
Agent: Mhm—voicemail plus scrambling and putting people on hold is exactly that hectic overflow. Have you looked at anything yet to make sure every new buyer/seller call gets answered during the day?
User: No, not yet. That's why I'm interested in your service. Tell me more — this is exactly what I need!
Agent: Totally—Dialux is built to make sure those new buyer/seller calls get answered in the moment (even when the main line’s blowing up), so you’re not losing them to the next agent. Mind if I do a super quick 30‑second calculation to show what those ~25 missed calls a week could be costing you?
User: Sure, go ahead! I'm curious. Also, I'm so busy next week—actually, tomorrow works. Let's book it!
Agent: Got it—and we can talk booking right after this quick math. Of those ~25 missed/voicemail calls a week, what percent do you think would turn into a signed client if you answered—like 20%, 40%, 60%?
User: I'd say around 40% could turn into signed clients if we actually answered them right away.
Agent: Got it—40%. And what’s the average commission you actually take home per signed client from these calls (rough ballpark)?
User: Around $5,000 per transaction, give or take. It really adds up when you miss out on those calls!
Agent: Got it—at 25 missed calls a week, 40% conversion, and ~$5,000 per deal, that’s about **$50,000/week**, or roughly **$216,500/month** in missed revenue.

Cool. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—Jay will show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on; what’s better for you: later today or tomorrow?
User: Wow, that's insane! Tomorrow works for sure. Can you confirm the exact time again? I changed my day.
Agent: Makes sense—what exact time tomorrow works for you, and which time zone are you in (Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific)?
User: Oh, I'm in Central time. Let's go with 2 PM. Can you confirm that for me?
Agent: Got it—Central time, 2 PM tomorrow. Before I can lock anything in, what’s your last name?
User: My last name's Martinez. So we're set for tomorrow at 2 PM Central? Let me know if that's confirmed!
Agent: Got it, Sofia Martinez. What’s the best phone number to text the confirmation to?
User: Text me at 832-555-1234. Looking forward to the call! Thanks for setting this up.
Agent: Thanks, Sofia—got it: 832-555-1234. I can do tomorrow (Wednesday) at **12:15 PM** or **2:30 PM** Central time—which one do you want?
User: Let's go with 2:30 PM Central. Please confirm that time is booked. Thanks!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: My calendar is giving me trouble right now—let me try that again.
Agent: I’m having trouble confirming the calendar right now—but I’ve got tomorrow at 2:30 PM Central in mind. We’ll reach you at 832-555-1234 within the hour to lock it in. Thanks, Sofia—talk soon.
